Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11294
DELEGATING CERTAIN AUTHORITY OF THE PRESIDENT TO ESTABLISH
MAXIMUM PER DIEM RATES FOR GOVERNMENT CIVILIAN PERSON­
NEL IN TRAVEL STATUS
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 of 
the United States Code, and as President of the United States, it is 
ordered as follows:
S ection  1. Executive Order No. 10621 of July 1, 1955, entitled 
“Delegation of Certain Functions of the President to the Secretary of 
Defense,” is hereby amended by adding the following paragraph at the 
end of Section 1 thereof:
“ (o) The authority vested in the President by section 3 of the Travel 
Expense Act of 1949,63 Stat. 166, as amended (5 U.S.C. 836), to estab­
lish maximum rates of per diem allowances for civilian officers and 
employees of the Government to the extent that such authority per­
tains to travel status in localities in Alaska, Hawaii, the Common­
wealth of Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone, and possessions of the United 
States.”
S ec. 2. -There is hereby delegated to the Secretary of State the 
authority vested in the President by Section 3 of the Travel Expense 
Act of 1949, 63 Stat. 166, as amended (5 U.S.C. 836), to establish 
maximum rates of per diem allowances for civilian officers and em­
ployees of the Government to the extent that such authority pertains 
to travel status in localities in any area (including the Trust Territory 
of the Pacific Islands) situated outside the United States, the Common­
wealth of Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone, and the possessions of the 
United States.
S ec. 3. Executive Order No. 11230 of June 28,1965, entitled “Dele­
gating Certain Functions of the President to the Director of the 
Bureau of the Budget,” as amended, is hereby further amended by 
substituting for paragraph (9) of Section 1 thereof the following:
“ (9) The authority vested in the President by Section 3 of the 
Travel Expense Act of 1949, 63 Stat. 166 (5 U.S.C. 836}, to establish 
maximum rates of per diem allowances for civilian officers and em­
ployees of the Government to the extent that such authority pertains 
to travel status of such officers and employees while en route to, from, 
or between localities situated outside the 48 contiguous states of the 
United States and the District of Columbia.”
S ec. 4. T o the extent not heretofore superseded, Executive Order 
No. 10970 of October 27,1961, is hereby superseded.
L yndon  B. J ohnson
T he  W h ite H ouse,
August 4 >  1966.
[F.R. Doc. 66-8687; Filed, Aug. 5, 1966, 2:03 p.m.]
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 31, NO. 153— TUESDAY, AUGUST 9, 1966

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sec. 1 is a self-executing amendment: EO 10621 "is hereby amended by adding the following paragraph at the end of Section 1 thereof" (paragraph (o)). It was complete on signing, August 4, 1966; no later effective date appears. The paragraph continued inside EO 10621 until EO 12561 Sec. 1 revoked "the current subsection (o)" and EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294 on July 1, 1986; EO 12396 (1982) did not revoke paragraph (o). The 1986 revocation is a later event for this clause, not its first end.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sec. 2 delegates to the Secretary of State the authority vested in the President by Section 3 of the Travel Expense Act of 1949 (5 U.S.C. 836) to establish maximum per diem rates for travel status in areas outside the United States. It is a continuing delegation. EO 12561 Sec. 3 reads "Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4,1966, is revoked." and, in its Sec. 2, delegates to the Secretary of State the successor authority under Section 102(a) of the 1985 Act (5 U.S.C. 5702(a)) for the same areas. The order states no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, July 1, 1986. EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) superseded only Section 3 of EO 11294, so Sec. 2 is not shown to have ended earlier.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sec. 3 is a self-executing amendment of EO 11230: paragraph (9) of Section 1 is substituted by new text delegating the per diem authority for travel outside the 48 contiguous States to the Bureau of the Budget. It was complete on signing, August 4, 1966. EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) then superseded "Section 3 of Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966" with immediate effect under its Sec. 12 (July 22, 1971), and EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294 on July 1, 1986. Both are later events; they are not the first end of a command that was spent on issue.

research_rationale:
EO 11294 (31 FR 10601, signed 1966-08-04) has four sections. Sec. 1 adds paragraph (o) to Section 1 of EO 10621 (per diem delegation to the Secretary of Defense for Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone and possessions); Sec. 3 substitutes paragraph (9) of Section 1 of EO 11230; Sec. 4 supersedes EO 10970 to the extent not already superseded. Each is a self-executing amendment or supersession spent on signing, 1966-08-04. Sec. 2 is a continuing delegation to the Secretary of State of the President's per diem authority for areas outside the United States; it ended on 1986-07-01 when EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294, in the same order that re-delegated the successor authority to the Secretary of State (Sec. 2) and revoked paragraph (o) of EO 10621 (Sec. 1). EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) superseded only Section 3 on 1971-07-22. The latest clause end, 1986-07-01, is the whole-order end. No held text shows an earlier end of Sec. 2, and the bounded searches found no other instrument naming EO 11294 as amended or revoked.

For Sec. 2, the held orders that name EO 11294 are EO 11609 (Sec. 11(5) supersedes only Section 3) and EO 12561 (Sec. 3 revokes the whole order); EO 12396 amends EO 10621 but leaves paragraph (o) and names no part of EO 11294. EO 11609 Sec. 1(2) delegates the 5 U.S.C. 5702(a) per diem authority outside the 48 contiguous states to the Office of Management and Budget; it does not name or supersede Sec. 2 and is not shown to extinguish it. The text of the 1985 Act (Pub. L. 99-234) and of 5 U.S.C. 5702 and 5707 is not held, so a statutory change before 1986-07-01 is not excluded by statute text; the end is therefore claimed from the express revocation in EO 12561 together with its successor delegation, and no held source shows an earlier lapse.","independent_command_check":"Sec. 2 is the only command with its own continuing force; Secs. 1, 3 and 4 act on other orders and ended on issue, with their consequences continuing inside the parent orders. Sec. 2 stands independently of Sec. 3: the supersession of Sec. 3 by EO 11609 did not touch it.","savings_check":"EO 12561 contains no savings clause for acts under EO 11294 in its Sec. 1 to 3. Rates already fixed under the delegation are accrued results; paragraph (o) and paragraph (9) lived in the parent orders, as stated in the savings reason.","scope_check":"Four clauses, matching the four sections of the held Federal Register text: Sec. 1 (amends EO 10621), Sec. 2 (delegation to the Secretary of State), Sec. 3 (amends EO 11230), Sec. 4 (supersedes EO 10970). The only partial change is EO 11609 Sec. 11(5), which reaches Sec. 3 alone. Note: the Federal Register disposition note names the superseded order as EO 10960, while the held text of Sec. 4 reads \"Executive Order No. 10970\"; the claim follows the held text."}

savings_residuals.reason: Paragraph (o) added by Sec. 1 continued inside EO 10621 until EO 12561 Sec. 1 revoked "the current subsection (o)" on 1986-07-01, and paragraph (9) substituted by Sec. 3 continued in EO 11230 until EO 11609 superseded that parent on 1971-07-22; both are consequences in the parent orders, not continuing commands of EO 11294. The Sec. 2 delegation was replaced by the delegation in EO 12561 Sec. 2 under the 1985 Act. Per diem rates fixed under the delegation are accrued results.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the  
United States of America, including Section 102(a) of the Federal Civilian  
Employee and Contractor Travel Expenses A ct of 1985 (Public Law 99— 234)  
(“the A ct” )  and Section 301 of Title 3  of the United States Code, it is ordered  
as follows:
Section 1. Section 1  of Executive Order No. 10621 of July 1, 1955, as amended,  
is further amended by redesignating the current subsection (i) as subsection
(g); by revoking the current subsection (o); and by adding the following new  
subsection (h):
“ (h) The authority vested in the President by Section 102(a) of the Federal  
Civilian Employee and Contractor Travel Expenses A ct of 1985, 5  U .S .C .  
5702(a), to establish maximum rates of per diem allowances and reimburse­
ments for the actual and necessary expenses of official travel for employees of  
the Government to the extent that such authority pertains to travel status in  
localities in Alaska, Hawaii, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and posses­
sions of the United States.”
Sec. 2. There is hereby delegated to the Secretary of State the authority vested  
in the President by Section 102(a) of the A ct (5 U .S .C . 5702(a)) to establish  
maximum rates of per diem allowances and reimbursements for the actual and  
necessary expenses o f official travel for employees of the Government to the  
extent that such authority pertains to travel status in localities (including the  
Trust Territories of the Pacific Islands) in any area situated outside the United  
States, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and the possessions of the United  
States.
Sec. 3. Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4,1966, is revoked.
